summary.headline: The Planning Board approved public tree removals, required six replacement trees for an unauthorized removal on Route 9, and reviewed native planting standards.
summary.summary: The Planning Board conducted joint hearings with the tree warden to approve four public tree removals and one trimming, and required six three-inch caliper replacement trees for an unauthorized tree removal at 154 Turnpike Road. The board received an update on resolving site conditions and extending the temporary occupancy permit for 40-42 Central Street. Members also reviewed a proposed native plant and invasive species policy presented by the Open Space Preservation Commission and heard an update on Master Plan implementation.

topics.title: 40-42 Central Street site status update
topics.summary: Historical Board member and project representative John Delli Priscoli provided an update on resolving site plan discrepancies at 40-42 Central Street, including preparation of an as-built plan by an engineer and establishing escrow for third-party peer review. Discussion focused on parking spaces, van-accessible handicap spaces, entrance railings, and deed restrictions regarding dedicated and flex spaces. The board voted to recommend extending the temporary occupancy permit through May 11, 2026, to allow time for as-built filings and review.
key_details: Engineer is preparing a three-sheet as-built comparison plan overlaid on approved conditions.
Discussions covered parking stall dimensions, signage for town-reserved spaces, and front entrance railings.
An escrow retainer check is being provided to town staff for third-party engineering review.
The board recommended the building commissioner extend the temporary occupancy permit to May 11, 2026.
topics.outcome: Recommended extension of the temporary occupancy permit through May 11, 2026.

topics.title: Public hearing on DPW scenic road tree removals
topics.summary: The Planning Board and Tree Warden held a joint public hearing on a DPW application to remove four trees and trim one tree along designated scenic roads. The list included removals at 34 Oregon Road (14-inch hickory), 28 Lovers Lane (36-inch oak), 202 Woodland Road (36-inch pine), and 21 Newton Road (24-inch maple), plus trimming of a 40-foot oak at 62 Mount Vickery Road. The board closed the hearing and voted to approve all removals and the trimming as proposed.
key_details: Four trees approved for removal due to decay, cavities, insect damage, and public safety hazards.
One 40-foot oak tree at 62 Mount Vickery Road approved for selective branch trimming away from a residence.
No written objections were received prior to the hearing.
Board and tree warden discussed efforts to build a GIS layer tracking town tree inventory and planting locations.
topics.outcome: Approved unanimous removal of four trees and trimming of one tree.

topics.title: 22 Turnpike Road major site plan modification
topics.summary: The board considered a continuation request for the major site plan approval modification at 22 Turnpike Road (golf range). The applicant requested continuing the public hearing without testimony to May 11, 2026. The board voted to extend the decision deadline to June 6, 2026, and continued the hearing.
key_details: Project location: 22 Turnpike Road (golf range).
Action deadline extended to June 6, 2026.
Hearing continued to May 11, 2026, at 6:45 PM without testimony.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to May 11, 2026; action deadline extended to June 6, 2026.

topics.title: 154 Turnpike Road unauthorized tree removal hearing
topics.summary: The board held a joint public hearing with the tree warden regarding the unauthorized removal of a public shade tree at the corner of Turnpike Road and Breakneck Hill Road. Representatives of Capital Group Properties stated the tree was in decay and removed due to safety concerns during construction. The board and tree warden determined that proper procedure was not followed and agreed on mitigation requiring the developer to provide six three-inch caliper trees to be planted by the town.
key_details: Developer removed a 24-inch town shade tree without prior notice or public hearing.
Developer agreed to provide six 3-inch caliper replacement trees acceptable to the tree warden.
Replacement trees will be planted by the town at locations selected by the tree warden and DPW rather than the original roadside corner.
Board members emphasized that town trees cannot be removed by private parties regardless of perceived condition.
topics.outcome: Approved remediation requiring applicant to donate six 3-inch caliper replacement trees.
topics.why_it_matters: Enforces Southborough's public shade tree protections and ensures town canopy loss from unauthorized contractor removals is compensated through replacement plantings.

topics.title: Discussion of tree warden imminent hazard declarations
topics.summary: Board members raised concerns with the tree warden regarding trees declared imminent hazards under state law that remain standing for weeks or months before removal. The tree warden explained that the town lacks an internal tree crew, making immediate removal reliant on availability of outside tree contractors, utility coordination, police details, and weather. Members suggested reviewing contractor agreements to establish guaranteed response times for genuine emergency hazards.
key_details: State law allows tree wardens to bypass public hearings only if a tree poses an imminent hazard to health or property.
Members noted that if a hazard tree sits for weeks, it should have been posted for a hearing.
Tree warden noted logistical hurdles such as police details, road closures, cranes, and contractor availability.
A board member recommended establishing contractual rapid-response times for emergency tree takedowns.
topics.outcome: Discussion concluded with tree warden agreeing to explore tighter contractor coordination.

topics.title: 154 Turnpike Road major site plan modification
topics.summary: The applicant for 154 Turnpike Road requested a continuation of the major site plan approval modification hearing to allow additional time to finalize landscape plans submitted earlier that day. The board voted to continue the hearing to May 11, 2026, and extended its decision deadline to June 5, 2026.
key_details: Applicant submitted revised landscape plans on the morning of the meeting.
Hearing continued without testimony to May 11, 2026, at 7:00 PM.
Board action deadline extended to June 5, 2026.
topics.outcome: Hearing continued to May 11, 2026; action deadline extended to June 5, 2026.

topics.title: Native plant and invasive species landscape policy
topics.summary: Open Space Preservation Commission Chair Freddie Gillespie presented a comprehensive draft policy promoting native plantings, soft landings, and invasive species management in landscape designs under Planning Board review. Discussion covered ecological benefits to pollinators and birds, restrictions on neonicotinoids and systemic pesticides, and concerns regarding the use of stone mulch. Board members supported incorporating native planting standards into site plan rules and regulations while recommending that the complex invasive species management requirements be developed separately.
key_details: Proposal establishes standards requiring native species for landscape reviews based on Go Botany and Dr. Robert Gegear pollinator plant lists.
Proposes discouraging dyed mulch, landscape fabric, and stone mulch in favor of living ground covers and soft landings.
Recommends restrictions on plants treated with systemic pesticides and neonicotinoids.
Planning Board agreed to draft site plan regulations for native plants for adoption at their next meeting, while deferring the invasive management section for broader study.
topics.outcome: Agreed to draft native plant standards as formal site plan regulations for the May 11, 2026 meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: Changes landscape design rules for all future commercial and multi-family developments in Southborough by requiring ecologically beneficial native plants and restricting harmful landscaping materials.

topics.title: Master Plan Implementation Committee update
topics.summary: A board member provided an update on the Master Plan Implementation Committee, noting that many of the 200-plus goals from the 2021 plan are underway across town departments. The committee is beginning early discussions about initiating the next master plan cycle around 2028 for a 2030 target date and is exploring potential state One Stop Community grant funding to hire planning consultants.
key_details: Committee is tracking over 200 goals from the 2021 Master Plan.
Discussion began about pursuing a hybrid consultant model for the next plan targeting 2028-2030.
Town staff are evaluating state One Stop grant opportunities due in June for planning support.
Potential joint meeting with the Select Board will be scheduled to discuss long-term planning priorities.
topics.outcome: Informational update; committee will continue exploring grant funding options.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board received brief administrative updates from the town planner, noted a vacant seat on the Conservation Commission, and postponed approval of past meeting minutes before adjourning.
key_details: Conservation Commission has an open member vacancy.
Meeting minutes approval postponed to the next meeting.

Close the public hearing on the DPW scenic road tree removal list.
Approve the removal of four trees and trimming of one tree on scenic roads as presented in the DPW application dated April 9, 2026.
Extend the action deadline for 22 Turnpike Road major site plan modification to June 6, 2026.
Continue the public hearing for 22 Turnpike Road to May 11, 2026, at 6:45 PM.
Close the public hearing for the unauthorized tree removal at 154 Turnpike Road.
Approve mitigation for the unauthorized tree removal at 154 Turnpike Road consisting of six three-inch caliper replacement trees to be coordinated with the tree warden.
Continue the public hearing for 154 Turnpike Road major site plan modification to May 11, 2026, at 7:00 PM without testimony.
Extend the decision deadline for 154 Turnpike Road major site plan modification to June 5, 2026.

public_comment.summary: A resident of Lovers Lane asked about town priorities for removing hazard trees on streets that rely on private well water, noting that falling trees taking down power lines leave residents without domestic water or power for medical devices.
The Open Space Preservation Commission chair inquired about the status of replacement tree plantings owed to the town by utility companies from previous mass tree removals along scenic roads.
